1:1.t: Achaia: the Roman province of southern Greece, with Corinth its capital.

1:8.t: The trouble in Asia is not otherwise known; it may relate to the riot at Ephesus (Acts 19:23-41) or a severe illness.

2:1.t: "A painful visit": Paul had apparently made a second, sorrowful visit to Corinth not recorded in Acts.

2:4.t: This "tearful letter" was written between 1 and 2 Corinthians and has not survived, unless it is part of chapters 10-13.

2:5.t: The offender may be the man of 1 Corinthians 5, or someone who had opposed Paul during his painful visit.

5:17.t: "All things": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read simply "the new has come".
"New creation" (Greek kaine ktisis): the KJV's "a new creature". The phrase can mean that the believer is a new creation, or that in Christ the new creation of the age to come has begun.

6:12.t: "Affection": the KJV's "bowels"; Greek splanchna, the inner parts, thought of as the seat of feeling.

6:15.t: "Belial": a Hebrew word meaning "worthlessness", used as a name for Satan.

6:16.t: Quotations of Leviticus 26:12, Jeremiah 32:38, Ezekiel 37:27, Isaiah 52:11, Ezekiel 20:34, 2 Samuel 7:14 and 7:8.

8:18.t: This brother may have been Luke, but he is not named.

10:1.t: Many think these chapters may be part of a separate letter, perhaps the "tearful letter" of 2:4, because of their sharp change of tone. There is no manuscript evidence that the letter was ever divided.

11:3.t: "And pure": many early manuscripts add these words; the KJV does not have them.

11:5.t: "Super-apostles": the KJV's "the very chiefest apostles", meant ironically of Paul's rivals in Corinth.

11:24.t: The law limited a flogging to forty lashes (Deuteronomy 25:3); the Jews gave thirty-nine to avoid exceeding the limit by mistake.

11:25.t: "Beaten with rods": a Roman punishment (Acts 16:22). "Pelted with stones": see Acts 14:19.

11:31.t: "Of our Lord Jesus Christ": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "of the Lord Jesus".

11:32.t: Aretas IV was king of the Nabateans about 9 BC to AD 40. See Acts 9:23-25.

12:2.t: "The third heaven": the highest heaven, the dwelling of God, beyond the sky and the stars. Paul is speaking of himself.

13:11.t: "Farewell": the KJV's reading; Greek chairete, which can also mean "rejoice".

1:3.t: "Comfort" (Greek paraklesis, parakaleo): the word occurs ten times in these verses. It means comfort, encouragement and strengthening; see John 14:16.

1:22.t: "Seal ... deposit" (Greek sphragisamenos ... arrabon): the KJV's "sealed ... earnest". A seal marked ownership; an arrabon was a first installment guaranteeing full payment. The Spirit is God's guarantee of the salvation to come (5:5, Ephesians 1:14).

2:14.t: "Triumphal procession" (Greek thriambeuonti): the Roman victory parade, in which incense was burned and captives were led. Paul pictures himself as Christ's willing captive spreading the fragrance of the gospel.

2:17.t: "Peddle" (Greek kapeleuontes): the KJV's "corrupt", like a dishonest trader who waters down his wine.

3:6.t: "Covenant" (Greek diatheke): the KJV's "testament". See Matthew 26:28. "Letter ... Spirit" (Greek gramma ... pneuma): the law written on stone could command but not give life; the Spirit writes God's will on the heart (Jeremiah 31:33, Ezekiel 36:26-27).

3:14.t: "The old covenant" (Greek palaia diatheke): the KJV's "the old testament", meaning the covenant at Sinai read in the synagogue, the Law of Moses. This is the origin of the name "Old Testament".

3:17.t: "The Lord is the Spirit": in the Exodus story Moses turned to "the LORD"; Paul says that now the LORD is met through the Spirit. Paul does not merge the persons; he speaks of "the Spirit of the Lord" in the same verse.

3:18.t: "Reflect ... as in a mirror" (Greek katoptrizomenoi): either "behold as in a mirror" (the KJV) or "reflect like a mirror". "Transformed" (Greek metamorphoumetha): see Matthew 17:2.

4:4.t: "The god of this age": Satan (compare John 12:31). "Image" (Greek eikon): see Matthew 22:21. Christ is the perfect image of God, as Adam was meant to be.

4:7.t: "Jars of clay" (Greek ostrakinois skeuesin): the KJV's "earthen vessels", cheap, fragile pottery. The weakness of the container shows that the power belongs to God.

4:17.t: "Eternal glory that far outweighs" (Greek baros doxes): "weight of glory". In Hebrew the word for glory (kavod) comes from the word for "heavy".

5:1.t: "Tent ... building ... clothed": pictures of the present body and the resurrection body. Paul longs not for a bodiless existence but for the new body.

5:21.t: "Made Him ... to be sin for us": Christ bore the guilt and penalty of sin (Isaiah 53:6, 10). Some take "sin" here as "sin offering", as the Hebrew chatta'th means both. "The righteousness of God" (Greek dikaiosyne theou): see Romans 1:17.

6:14.t: "Yoked together" (Greek heterozygountes): to be harnessed with an animal of a different kind (Deuteronomy 22:10). Often applied to marriage, the command concerns any binding partnership that compromises faith.

7:10.t: "Godly sorrow ... worldly sorrow": godly sorrow leads to repentance (metanoia, see Matthew 3:2) and new life; worldly sorrow is mere regret or shame, which leads to despair.

8:1.t: "Grace" (Greek charis): Paul uses the word for the gift of money itself, as an act of grace flowing from God's grace.

8:6.t: "Grace" (Greek charis): Paul uses the word for the gift of money itself, as an act of grace flowing from God's grace.

8:9.t: "Though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor": a summary of the incarnation and the cross (compare Philippians 2:6-8).

9:7.t: "Cheerful" (Greek hilaron): the source of the English "hilarious", glad, willing.

9:15.t: "Indescribable gift" (Greek anekdiegetos dorea): the KJV's "unspeakable gift", God's gift of His Son.

10:4.t: "Strongholds ... arguments" (Greek ochyromata ... logismous): fortresses and reasonings. Paul's warfare is against ideas and pride raised against God.

11:2.t: "Godly jealousy" (Greek theou zelos): a jealousy like God's own for His people (Exodus 34:14, Hosea 2:19-20).

11:14.t: "Masquerades" (Greek metaschematizetai): the KJV's "is transformed", to change one's outward appearance, to disguise oneself.

11:30.t: "Weakness" (Greek astheneia): a key word in this letter. Paul boasts in what shows Christ's power, not his own (12:9-10).

12:7.t: "A thorn in my flesh" (Greek skolops te sarki): a sharp stake. Readers have suggested an eye disease (compare Galatians 4:13-15, 6:11), another illness, or persistent opposition. Paul does not say.

12:9.t: "Grace" (Greek charis): see Acts 15:11. "Made perfect" (Greek teleitai): brought to completion, shown in full.

13:5.t: "Fail the test" (Greek adokimoi): the KJV's "reprobates", rejected after testing, like counterfeit coins.

13:14.t: One of the clearest New Testament verses naming Father, Son and Holy Spirit together. "Fellowship" (Greek koinonia): the KJV's "communion"; the sharing that the Spirit creates, or sharing in the Spirit. See Acts 2:42.
